title: Little Office of S. John the Baptist
translationNotice: English translation prepared for Sacrum Florilegium; not supplied in the source PDF.

blocks.source: Fuit homo missus a Deo, cui nomen erat Joannes, hic venit in testimonium, ut testimonium perhiberet de lumine, ut omnes crederent per illum.
blocks.english: There was a man sent from God whose name was John. He came for a witness, to bear witness to the light, that all might believe through him.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine labia mea aperies.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, Thou shalt open my lips.

blocks.source: ℟. Et os meum annuntiabit laudem tuam.
blocks.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare Thy praise.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Praecursorem summi Regis Et Praeconem novae legis Coeli ornat gloria; Sed et ortus gratiosa, Nec non mortis pretiosa Terris est memoria.
blocks.english:
Heaven’s glory adorns
The forerunner of the highest King
And herald of the new law;
But on earth also the memory
Of his birth is gracious,
And of his death precious.

blocks.source: Pater senex novum natum Dandum stupet; dum legatum Audit missum coelitus; Nam aetatem et naturam Spectans, aegre rem futuram Credit jam decrepitus.
blocks.english:
The aged father marvels
That a new son is to be given,
When he hears the envoy sent from heaven;
For, considering age and nature,
Now decrepit, he scarcely believes
That the thing will come to pass.

blocks.source: Sed quod negat, quod infirmat, Hoc attestans mox confirmat Linguae destitutio; Dum non paret verbo parens, Jam ex perdita apparens Voce fit punitio.
blocks.english:
But what he denies and doubts,
The loss of speech soon confirms
By bearing witness;
When the parent obeys not the word,
Punishment now appears
In his lost voice.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: Ecce eris tacens, et non poteris loqui, pro eo quod non credidisti verbis meis, quae implebuntur in tempore suo.
blocks.english: Behold, thou shalt be silent and unable to speak, because thou hast not believed my words, which shall be fulfilled in their time.

blocks.source: ℣. Tu puer Propheta altissimi vocaberis.
blocks.english: ℣. Thou, child, shalt be called the Prophet of the Most High.

blocks.source: ℟. Praeibis enim ante faciem Domini parare vias ejus.
blocks.english: ℟. For thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare His ways.

blocks.source: Oremus,
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: Deus, qui praesentem commemorationem honorabilem nobis in beati Joannis nativitate fecisti: da populis tuis spiritualium gratiam gaudiorum, et omnium fidelium mentes dirige in viam salutis aeternae. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum. Amen.
blocks.english: O God, who hast made this present commemoration honourable for us in the birth of blessed John, grant Thy peoples the grace of spiritual joys, and direct the minds of all the faithful into the way of everlasting salvation. Through our Lord Jesus Christ. Amen.

blocks.source: ℣. Domine exaudi, etc. Benedicamus, etc.
blocks.english: ℣. O Lord, hear, etc. Let us bless, etc.

blocks.source: ℟. Et Fidelium, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. And of the faithful, etc.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Praecursore nondum nato, Nedum partu referato, Dona clarent coelica, Nostro sole tunc exclusus, Verioris est perfusus, Luce solis mystica.
blocks.english:
The forerunner not yet born,
Not yet brought forth in birth,
Heavenly gifts shine;
Then excluded from our sun,
He is bathed in the mystical light
Of the truer Sun.

blocks.source: Prius novit diem verum, Quam nostrorum sit dierum Usus beneficio; Ille notus nondum natus, Nondum nascens est renatus Christi ex commercio.
blocks.english:
He knows the true Day before
He enjoys the benefit of our days;
Known, though not yet born,
Not yet coming to birth, he is born anew
Through his encounter with Christ.

blocks.source: Alvo Deum Virgo claudit, Clauso clausus hic applaudid, Ventris ex custodia; Linguae gestus obsequuntur, Dum infantum colloquuntur Muta jam prodigia.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “applaudid”; the rejoicing reading is provisional. The contrast of the two enclosed children is retained.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: Ut audivit salutationem Elisabeth, exultavit infans in utero ejus, et repleta est Spiritu Sancto.
blocks.english: When Elisabeth heard the greeting, the infant leaped in her womb, and she was filled with the Holy Ghost.

blocks.source: ℣. Beata quae credidisti, quoniam perficientur.
blocks.english: ℣. Blessed art thou who hast believed, for there shall be fulfilled

blocks.source: ℟. Quae dicta sunt tibi a Domino.
blocks.english: ℟. The things spoken to thee by the Lord.

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Mater parit; Pater credit; Reduente fide, redit Linguae beneficium. Eja felix partus Matris, Quo soluta lingua Patris Celebrat mysterium.
blocks.english:
The mother gives birth, the father believes;
With faith returning, the gift of speech returns.
O happy birth of the mother,
Whereby the father’s tongue, set free,
Celebrates the mystery!
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “Reduente”; returning faith is a provisional reading.

blocks.source: Thori fructus Matri dantur; Ejam Matris expiantur Sterilis opprobria; Ortu tanti praecursoris Multi timent, sed timoris Comes est laetitia.
Se de munde servans mundum, Munde vivit intra mundum In aetate tenera, Sed e mundi mox convictu Cedens, loco, veste, vietu Mera perfert aspera!
blocks.english:
Keeping himself pure from the world,
He lives purely within the world
In tender age;
But soon departing from its society,
In place, dress and food
He bears nothing but hardships.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “munde” and “vietu”; the pure/food readings are provisional.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: Erat Joannes vestitus pilis camelii, et zona pellicea circa lumbos ejus, et locustas et mel sylvestre edebat.
blocks.english: John was clothed in camel’s hair, with a leather girdle about his loins, and ate locusts and wild honey.

blocks.source: ℣. Erit magnus coram Domino.
blocks.english: ℣. He shall be great before the Lord.

blocks.source: ℟. Et vinum et siceram non bibet.
blocks.english: ℟. And shall drink neither wine nor strong drink.

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Lege vitae sub angusta Mel sylvestre cum locusta, Cibum non abhorruit; Camelorum tectus pilis, Per desertum mundo vilis, Coelo magnus claruit.
blocks.english:
Under a strict rule of life
He did not shun wild honey
And locusts as food;
Clothed in camel’s hair,
In the desert, lowly to the world,
He shone great before heaven.

blocks.source: Quem dum replet lux superna, Verae lucis fit lucerna: Veri solis Lucifer. Novus novae praecone legis, Imo novus novi Regis Pugnatur signifer.
blocks.english:
When heavenly light fills him,
He becomes a lamp of the true Light,
The morning star of the true Sun;
A new herald of the new law,
Indeed of the new King
A new champion and standard-bearer.
blocks.editorialNote: “praecone” and “Pugnatur signifer” are irregular; the herald/champion readings are provisional.

blocks.source: Singulari Prophetia Prophetarum Monarchia Sublimatur omnium: Hi venturum, hic praesentem, Hi promissum, hic viventem Monstrat orbis Dominum.
blocks.english:
By a singular prophecy
He is raised above
All the rule of the prophets;
They show the Lord of the world to come,
He shows Him present; they promised,
He living.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed final contrast has compressed syntax; it is retained without adding an external prophetic text.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: Vidit Joannes Jesum, et ait: Ecce Agnus Dei, ecce qui tollit peccata mundi.
blocks.english: John saw Jesus and said: Behold the Lamb of God; behold Him who takes away the sins of the world.

blocks.source: ℣. Et audierunt eum discipuli.
blocks.english: ℣. And the disciples heard him,

blocks.source: ℟. Et secuti sunt Jesum.
blocks.english: ℟. And followed Jesus.

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Ardens vita, verbo lucens; Et ad veram lucem ducens Multa docet milia, O quam clarus mos docendi, Cum doctoris dant vivendi Formulam vestigia!
blocks.english:
Burning in life, shining in word,
And leading to the true Light,
He teaches many thousands;
O how splendid a manner of teaching,
When the teacher’s footsteps give
The pattern of living!

blocks.source: Non lux quidem fuit iste, Sed ut daret tibi, Christe, Luci testimonium. Non lux erat, sed lucerna: Verbum Christus luc aeterma, Lucem cerans omnium.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “luc aeterma” and “Lucem cerans omnium.” Eternal light is provisional, and the final clause unresolved.

blocks.source: Dum baptizat Christum soris, Reddit Christus dignioris Aquae beneficium; En! ut ambos curat Numen! Isti Flamen, illi flumen Addidit praeconium.
blocks.english:
While he baptizes Christ [the printed “soris” is unresolved],
Christ gives the benefit
Of a more worthy water;
Behold how the Godhead cares for both!
To this one the Spirit, to that the river
Added praise.
blocks.editorialNote: “soris” is unresolved. The division of praise between Spirit and river is kept as printed, without assigning an invented subject.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: In diebus illis venit Jesus a Nazareth Galilaeae, et baptizatus est a Joanne in Jordane.
blocks.english: In those days Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee and was baptized by John in the Jordan.

blocks.source: ℣. Ego baptizo vos aqua.
blocks.english: ℣. I baptize you with water.

blocks.source: ℟. Ille vero baptizabit vos Spiritu Sancto.
blocks.english: ℟. But He shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost.

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

blocks.source: Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Qui baptizat, elevatur, Baptizatus non lavatur, In quo nulla macula, Aquae lavant, quin lavantur, Quaeis lavandi vires dantur, Vi mundantis omnia.
Contemplatur omnes istum, Quem putabat turba Christum, Stupens ad prodigia, Qui cervicem non erexit, Sed Dominum se despexit, Domini corrigia.
blocks.english:
All behold him whom the crowd
Thought to be Christ,
Amazed at the wonders;
He did not raise his neck in pride,
But [the printed “Sed Dominum se despexit” is uncertain],
At the Lord’s sandal-strap.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “Contemplatur omnes” and “Sed Dominum se despexit, Domini corrigia”; the latter clause is uncertain and not silently repaired.

blocks.source: Attestante palam Christo: Non surrexit major isto Natus de muliere, Solum Christus se excepit, Qui de carne carnem cept. Sine carnis opere.
blocks.english:
Christ openly bearing witness:
No one born of woman
Has arisen greater than he;
Christ alone excepted Himself,
Who took flesh from flesh
Without the work of the flesh.
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “cept”; took flesh is provisional. Its Christ-exception statement remains the source’s claim.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: Amen dico vobis, inter natos mulierum non surrexit major Joanne Baptista.
blocks.english: Amen, I say to you: among those born of women there has not arisen one greater than John the Baptist.

blocks.source: ℣. Quid existis videre Prophetam?
blocks.english: ℣. What did you go out to see, a Prophet?

blocks.source: ℟. Ego dico vobis, etiam plusquam Prophetam.
blocks.english: ℟. I say to you, yea, more than a Prophet.

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

referenceExpansion.note: The printed incipit repeats the specified prayer group from this office only. Printed abbreviations and source-reading warnings in the target remain.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Non hic Praeco veritatis, Ut arundo levitatis, Quaevis laudat placita; Sed et scribas, et Doctores, Vocat legis et ruptores, Viperae genimina.
blocks.english:
This herald of truth does not,
Like a reed of fickleness,
Praise every pleasure;
But calls scribes and teachers,
And breakers of the law,
A brood of vipers.

blocks.source: Quin et arguit Herodem, Unde vinctus ab eodem, Sed nec victus carcere; Fert injustam justus poenam, Rem detestans, vah! obscenam Regis et adulterae.
blocks.english:
Nay, he reproves Herod,
And so is bound by him,
Yet not conquered by prison;
The just man bears an unjust punishment,
Abhorring the shameful affair
Of the king and the adulteress.

blocks.source: Inde saevit vis Tyranni, Sed ut crevite laus Joanni, Regi sic supplicium, Servit stultus nam prudenti, Dum probatur in persenti Innocens per impium.
blocks.english:
Hence the tyrant’s violence rages,
But as praise of John increased,
So did punishment for the king;
For the fool serves the prudent,
While in the present the innocent
Is proved by the wicked.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “crevite” and “persenti” are defective; increased/present are provisional readings.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: Herodes autem, cum corriperetur ab illo de Herodiade uxore fratris sui, adjecit et hoc super omnia, et inclusit Joannem in carcere.
blocks.english: But Herod, being reproved by him concerning Herodias, his brother’s wife, added this also above all things, and shut John in prison.

blocks.source: ℣. Volens illum occidere timuit populum.
blocks.english: ℣. Wishing to kill him, he feared the people,

blocks.source: ℟. Quia sicut Prophetam habebant eum.
blocks.english: ℟. For they held him as a Prophet.

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

blocks.source: ℣. Converte nos Deus salutaris noster.
blocks.english: ℣. Convert us, O God our Saviour.

blocks.source: ℟. Et averte iram tuam a nobis.
blocks.english: ℟. And turn away Thine anger from us.

blocks.source: ℣. Deus in adjutorium meum intende.
blocks.english: ℣. O God, come to my assistance.

blocks.source: ℟. Domine ad adjuvandum me festina. Gloria Patri, etc.
blocks.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me. Glory be to the Father, etc.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: In natalis sui coena, Capitali plecti poena Rex Joannem jusserat, Spiculator saltatrici, Laena desert Genitrici Caput quod petierat;
blocks.english:
At his birthday feast
The king had ordered John
To be punished by beheading;
The executioner [the printed “Laena desert” is unresolved]
To the dancing girl and her mother
The head which she had asked for.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed “Laena desert Genitrici” is unresolved; no verb of giving is invented to complete it.

blocks.source: Crux designat sublimari Christum, sed hunc minorari Capitis abscissio.
blocks.english:
The Cross signifies Christ’s being raised,
But the cutting off of the head
This man’s being made less.

blocks.source: O mors vere pretiosa Prae quoa est tam gloriosa Vitae conversatio!
blocks.english:
O death truly precious,
Before which the conduct
Of his life is so glorious!
blocks.editorialNote: The source prints “quoa”; the English connection is provisional.

blocks.source: Atque haec in laudem, Christe! Tu reddimus Baptistae Vota, et encomia, Nos ad vitam recto calle Ex hac mortis ducas valle Ejus ut per merita.
blocks.english:
And these vows and praises of the Baptist
We render to Thy praise, O Christ,
That through his merits
Thou mayest lead us by the straight path
From this valley of death
Unto life.

blocks.source: Antiphona
blocks.english: Antiphon

blocks.source: Misso spiculatore praecepit afferri caput ejus, et decollavit eum in carcere, et attulit caput ejus in disco.
blocks.english: Sending an executioner, he commanded his head to be brought; and he beheaded him in prison and brought his head on a dish.

blocks.source: ℣. Venerunt discipuli ejus, et tulerunt corpus ejus.
blocks.english: ℣. His disciples came and took his body,

blocks.source: ℟. Et posuerunt illud in monumento.
blocks.english: ℟. And laid it in a tomb.

blocks.source: Oratio ut supra.
blocks.english: Prayer as above.

blocks.source: Hymnus
blocks.english: Hymn

blocks.source: Caput sacrum dum truncatur, Et Herodi praesentatur In fatali phiala, Aures claudis atque ora, Cassa vultus et aurora, Dive claudis lumina, Sed quid nobis denum erit, Caput nostrum si mors ferit! Urget ira Judicis? Ni tu audias clamantes, Ni respicias peccantes, Reos mi defenderis! Audi ergo, interpella, Ut gehennae ex procella Caput nostrum eruas, Christus sed benigne donet, Ne in illud dira tonet, Sedes nobis coelicas.
blocks.english:
When thy holy head is cut off
And presented to Herod
In the fatal dish,
Thou dost close ears and mouth,
[The printed “Cassa vultus et aurora” is unresolved.]
O saint, thou dost close thine eyes.
But what at last shall become of us
If death strikes our head?
Does the Judge’s wrath press upon us?
Unless thou hear those who cry,
Unless thou look upon sinners,
[The printed “Reos mi defenderis” is uncertain.]
Hear, therefore, intercede,
That from the storm of hell
Thou mayest rescue our head;
But may Christ graciously give us
Heavenly dwellings,
Lest He thunder dreadful things against it.
blocks.editorialNote: “Cassa vultus et aurora” is unresolved; “denum” and “Reos mi defenderis” are defective. The readable petitions remain, with uncertain clauses identified.

blocks.source: ℣. Ora pro nobis Sancte Joannes Baptista.
blocks.english: ℣. Pray for us, Saint John the Baptist.

blocks.source: ℟. Ut digni efficiamur promissionibus Christi.
blocks.english: ℟. That we may be made worthy of the promises of Christ.

blocks.source: Oremus
blocks.english: Let us pray,

blocks.source: O Sancte Joannes Baptista, electe Praecursor et Angele Dei, qui venisti ante faciem Domini parare vias ejus, ostendens Agnum Dei, Dominum et Salvatorem nostrum, qui tollit peccata mundi: Intercede, quaesumus, pro nobis ad Dominum, ut sicut sanctitate nemini minor, humilitate omnibus major, Prophetarum potissimus, primus Martyrum exstitisti, ita, quem praedicando humiliter praecurristi, ejusdem fideliter mandata sequendo, vitam capiamus aeternam. Per eundem Christum Dominum nostrum, cui cum Patre et Spiritu Sancto vivit et regnat Deus in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: O Saint John the Baptist, chosen forerunner and angel of God, who camest before the face of the Lord to prepare His ways, showing the Lamb of God, our Lord and Saviour, who takes away the sins of the world, intercede, we beseech thee, for us with the Lord; that as thou wast inferior to none in holiness, greater than all in humility, chief of the prophets and first of the martyrs, so, faithfully following the commandments of Him whom thou didst humbly precede in preaching, we may attain everlasting life. Through the same Christ our Lord, [the printed “cui cum Patre et Spiritu Sancto vivit et regnat Deus” is grammatically defective] who with the Father and the Holy Ghost liveth and reigneth, God, world without end. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed conclusion begins “cui cum Patre ...”; its syntax is defective. The preceding titles, including first of the martyrs, are retained as source statements.

editorialNotes.text: All printed pages of this office were visually compared. Original Latin, existing English, printed hours and abbreviated conclusions are retained. Prepared English hymn stanzas preserve meaningful line divisions. Defective source readings remain explicitly provisional or unresolved. All eight printed hours remain. Seven prayer references expand the Matins collect from this office; the unique final prayer to the Baptist remains separate. Printed abbreviated concluding versicles remain abbreviated. No missing narratives or corrupt hymn clauses are supplied from another edition.
